decisions.reason: SOL's "spotless" intensifies 깨끗한 (clean) without source support; equal quality, so keep BASE.
새록새록 means memories surfacing one by one/gradually; SOL's "come flooding back" implies a sudden rush, shifting the tempo.
"came to a hotel" is the natural deictic choice for a narrator recounting this from inside the hotel; faithful.
The period gives the deadpan beat that matches 세상에, while losing nothing.
"sounded like" recasts 이렇게 말하니까 ... 기분 naturally; "Then again" matches 아니.
"Jinho hyung" keeps the name-then-title order used with "Kkeokjeong Hyung-nim"; "champion snorer" naturally renders 한 코골이 하는.
"thrown out" is idiomatic for 강제 퇴실; "bright voice" is acceptable for 시원시원한.
"made sure to" and "straighten" are natural and preserve the checking/fixing of 옷매무새.
BASE drops the 물끄러미 (gazing steadily) beat; SOL captures it and reads better.
Concise, natural, and faithful to 잠을 설쳐서.

뭐 잘못됐냐는 눈빛 is her puzzled "what's wrong?" look; SOL conveys that, BASE suggests she suspects wrongdoing.
Both faithful; SOL's phrasing and rhythm read more naturally.

"as long as" matches the 함께라면 construction.
"Guild group chat" matches the word order of 길드 단체 채팅방 and reads cleaner.

Fronted participial phrase mirrors 나를 두고 ... 돌아섰다 and improves rhythm.

BASE is punchier and preserves the 뒷모습 call-and-repetition with the preceding gaze.
